story.title: Fatal Pile-Up on Bulgarian Highway Claims Lives and Injures Many
story.summary: A severe pile-up involving approximately 50 vehicles occurred on a foggy motorway near Yambol, Bulgaria, resulting in at least 12 fatalities and numerous injuries. Emergency services, including police and paramedics, were deployed to assist at the scene. The crashes were attributed to thick fog conditions.

explore_lenses.label: Why does this crash matter beyond Yambol?
explore_lenses.title: It underscores Bulgaria's road-safety burden
explore_lenses.summary: The pile-up comes as Bulgaria continues to record one of the European Union's highest road-fatality rates, even though its longer-term trend has improved. Its scale also prompted a multi-agency emergency response across southeastern Bulgaria.

claims.text: The European Commission recorded 456 road deaths in Bulgaria in 2025, or 71 per million people—the highest rate in the EU that year.
The Commission says Bulgaria is among only five EU countries on course for the bloc's 2030 target of halving road deaths and serious injuries, despite its still-high fatality rate.

The government said emergency medical teams, military medical personnel, police and soldiers were assisting, with injured people taken to hospitals in Sliven, Yambol and Burgas and aircraft prepared for possible transfers to Sofia.

explore_lenses.label: What caused the two pile-ups?
explore_lenses.title: Fog is the leading explanation, not a final finding
explore_lenses.summary: Officials have linked the crashes to suddenly dense fog and sharply reduced visibility, but the collision sequence and any driver, vehicle or road factors remain under formal investigation. Authorities treat the events in the two carriageways as separate crashes that may share a cause.

claims.text: Interior Ministry chief secretary Lyubomir Nikolov said the likely cause was sudden dense fog that sharply reduced visibility; local reporting cited witnesses who said visibility fell from roughly 70-80 metres to about 10 metres.
Nikolov's preliminary account was that a truck obstructed a passenger bus in the Burgas-bound lanes, after which further collisions followed; another crash occurred in the Sofia-bound lanes.
The prosecution says its investigation is intended to determine the causes; it has not publicly assigned legal responsibility to a driver, company or road authority.

story_report.summary: A multi-vehicle pile-up on a foggy motorway near Yambol, Bulgaria, killed at least 12 people and injured dozens. Around 50 vehicles were involved, prompting a large emergency response as authorities moved casualties to hospitals and prepared for possible transfers to Sofia.

sections.heading: Emergency Response and Hospital Transfers
sections.body: The government said emergency medical teams, military medical personnel, police and soldiers were assisting at the crash scene. Injured people were taken to hospitals in Sliven, Yambol and Burgas, while aircraft were placed on standby in case patients needed to be transferred to Sofia.

sections.heading: Fog Cited in Preliminary Account
sections.body: Interior Ministry chief secretary Lyubomir Nikolov said sudden dense fog was the likely cause, sharply reducing visibility. Local reporting cited witnesses who said visibility fell from about 70-80 metres to roughly 10 metres. Nikolov's preliminary account said a truck obstructed a passenger bus in the Burgas-bound lanes before further collisions followed, while another crash occurred in the Sofia-bound lanes.

sections.heading: Bulgaria's Road Safety Record
sections.body: The European Commission recorded 456 road deaths in Bulgaria in 2025, a rate of 71 per million people and the highest in the European Union that year. Despite the rate, the Commission said Bulgaria was among five EU countries on course to meet the bloc's 2030 target of halving road deaths and serious injuries.

unresolved.text: The final number and severity of injuries were still changing in initial official and media updates.

Prosecutors are investigating the causes and have not publicly assigned legal responsibility to any driver, company or road authority; the official cause will depend on technical and forensic findings.

related_stories.title: Explosion at Turkey Steel Factory Claims 17 Lives
related_stories.summary: A powerful explosion at the Habaş iron and steelworks in Aliağa, Izmir province, Turkey, has resulted in the deaths of at least 17 people. Eyewitnesses reported that the blast felt like an earthquake, with flames and thick smoke visible from the site. Distressed relatives gathered outside the factory following the incident.

related_stories.title: Rwandan Genocide Suspect Deported from U.S. to Face Trial
related_stories.summary: Jean Léonard Teganya has been deported from the United States to Rwanda, where he will stand trial for alleged genocide and crimes against humanity related to the 1994 Rwandan genocide. Rwandan prosecutors confirmed his arrival and the charges against him.

related_stories.title: French Police Investigate Mohamed Al Fayed Properties for Trafficking and Abuse
related_stories.summary: French police have conducted searches at several properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, as part of an investigation into an alleged international network trafficking women linked to Mohamed Al Fayed. Arrests have been made, and the inquiry focuses on claims of sexual abuse associated with the late businessman's ventures. Other properties in Paris and Saint-Tropez were also searched.

related_stories.title: The law criminalized consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples
related_stories.summary: A London court has overturned Trinidad and Tobago's law that criminalized consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. This decision marks a significant change in the legal landscape regarding LGBTQ+ rights in the country, which has been influenced by colonial-era laws.
